verdict.rationale: Supermemory's own MCP server documentation says users can 'Ask naturally' and the assistant picks the right Supermemory tool without code or tool names, so natural-language operation is a documented first-party capability. It works only through an external MCP-compatible assistant, and the evidence does not say which operations are covered. Missing for 10: a native natural-language interface in the product itself, documentation of which operations (add, search, delete, spaces) can be driven by natural language, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Ask naturally. The assistant selects the right Supermemory tool without requiring code or tool names.
Supermemory MCP gives every MCP-compatible assistant a shared memory layer, so technical and non-technical teams can collaborate with AI using the same authorized context.
